title: Parse time doubles with each nested `light-dark()` in a custom property

regression.note: performance regression from 6b5ac8b 'Handle light-dark with variables'; the rgb()/hsl() alpha variant is older (slow in 1.22.0 too)

impact: Found by OSS-Fuzz on a downstream tool (Fallow); no human-written CSS nests light-dark() 20 deep. No reactions. Matters as denial of service for services processing untrusted CSS: release 1.33.0 takes ~0.5 s at 20 levels and doubles per level, so a few hundred bytes hang the process. Not limited to custom properties: any typed property whose value falls back to tokens because of var() (e.g. `color:`, `width:`) is affected. Related finding: UnresolvedColor::parse restarts the token-list depth counter at 0, so nesting `light-dark(var(--a), ...` bypasses the 500-level guard and segfaults (stack overflow) 1.33.0 at 10,000 levels (#1297 family).
code: src/properties/custom.rs: TokenList::parse_into (try_parse(UnresolvedColor::parse) then generic Function fallback re-parses the same arguments)
src/properties/custom.rs: UnresolvedColor::parse ('light-dark', 'rgb', 'hsl' arms; nested TokenList::parse(input, options, 0) resets depth)
summary: For a function token, TokenList::parse_into first tries UnresolvedColor::parse, which fully parses the light-dark() arguments as token lists and only then fails (no comma, or an error token later). The generic function path then parses the same arguments again, so each nesting level doubles the work. The same happens through the rgb()/hsl() `/ alpha` path. The output is correct; only time is affected.
repro: triage/sweep/1382-repro.mjs (depths 18-20, 100 ms budget). Timings, 1.33.0 release vs master debug binding, `.a{--x:light-dark(x n var(--a) )x n}`: d10 0.8/9 ms, d15 16/270 ms, d20 463/8896 ms. Same shape in `color:` 801 ms and `width:` 435 ms at d20 (1.33.0). Unclosed `((((light-dark(` x20 1037 ms; `light-dark(red, ` x20 + `]` 1040 ms; `rgb(0 0 0 / ` x20 + `]` 1724 ms. Controls flat: valid `light-dark(..., blue)` nesting, nested var() fallbacks, rgb( without alpha.
evidence: perf scan with separate processes and 20 s timeout on local master and 1.33.0; repro.mjs --bisect 1.22.0..1.33.0: fast in 1.23.0, slow from 1.24.0 (light-dark cases); rgb alpha case slow in 1.22.0 too. git log -S finds 6b5ac8b 'Handle light-dark with variables'. Depth-guard bypass: `--x:` + `light-dark(var(--a), ` x3000 parses OK where `foo(` x600 errors with 'Overflowed the maximum nesting depth'; x10000 segfaults node with 1.33.0.

fix.approach: Parse light-dark() arguments once and decide afterwards whether it is a LightDark color or a generic Function (PR #1383); pass depth + 1 instead of 0. The rgb()/hsl() alpha arms need the same treatment (parse once, or propagate an error from the alpha token list instead of retrying), plus depth + 1.

openPRs.assessment: Fixes the light-dark() root cause: a dedicated parse_light_dark parses the arguments once, falls back to a Function without re-parsing when there is no comma, and propagates argument errors (a generic function would fail on the same tokens). It also passes depth + 1, which closes the depth-guard bypass for light-dark. Does not touch the rgb()/hsl() alpha path, which has the same exponential behaviour and still resets depth to 0; suggest extending it or a follow-up. Tests: round-trip cases and depth 40. CodSpeed shows no benchmark change. Not built.

draftReply:
Thanks for the report and the PR. Confirmed: on 1.33.0, `--x:` with 20 nested `light-dark(` around `var(--a)` takes about 0.5 s and doubles with each level; it started in 1.24.0 when `light-dark()` with variables was added. It also affects typed properties that contain `var()` (e.g. `color:`), and the same double parse happens through the alpha part of `rgb(0 0 0 / ...)` and `hsl()`. The output itself is correct.

There's an open PR, #1383, that addresses the `light-dark()` case; the `rgb()`/`hsl()` alpha path would need the same change.
